coverage.completeness_rule: at least 25 numeric October snow-precipitation days

supported: The predeclared negative snowfall-by-snow-prone-habitat interaction is not supported.
Adding October snowfall days and its interaction with published island habitat modestly improves in-sample R2 but worsens leave-one-year-out prediction.
The observed interaction coefficient is positive, opposite the predeclared directional prediction.
Litchfield remains the strongest negative local demographic deviation, but the available annual snowfall proxy does not explain that vulnerability in the predeclared interaction model.
not_supported: a simple annual snowfall amplification mechanism in which snow-prone islands perform relatively worse in snowier Octobers
causal attribution of island-specific demographic deviations to Palmer Station snowfall
a claim that terrestrial physical filtering is unimportant; only this annual proxy interaction is rejected
competitive interaction as an explanation for the residual island differences

synthesis_with_prior_stages.seaice_annual: not supported; positive directional sea-ice-duration mechanism failed
synthesis_with_prior_stages.remaining_pattern: strong common long-term decline plus substantial persistent and annual island heterogeneity remains unexplained by these simple linear annual/low-frequency forcing proxies

next_gate: Do not tune additional sea-ice-duration windows or precipitation months on the same outcome. Move to a distinct process hypothesis with externally defined predictors, such as breeding-habitat state/colony history or prey-mediated demographic pathways.
